text:
lin: heads up — saw a small but persistent p95 increase on canary for /v1/chat after the 11:15 rollout. Slice is 5%. Can someone pick this up? :mag:

deploy-bot: Canary rollout 11:15 -> 11:25: v4.1.0 at 5% traffic. Metrics: p95 +35%, tail queue time abnormal. Auto-rollback recommendation issued (latency_policy). Suggestion: soft withdraw.

sarah: I'm on traces. KV hit rate fine. Sampling shows longer scheduler wait with many short requests. Not a clear model delta.

lin: Given this is during the weekly change window, prefer pausing and doing a controlled withdraw instead of immediate full revert. Keep customers unaware unless impact grows.

eng_runtime_oncall: Agree. Let's do: 1) pause rollout; 2) withdraw canary (5->0) with staged drain; 3) pin route to last known good v3.9.7 for the window; 4) create an incident and attach traces. Who can run the commands?

sarah: I can run them. I'll run the traffic withdraw and pin.

deploy-bot: Suggested CLI:
```
deployctl pause --rollout r-98765
deployctl withdraw --rollout r-98765 --from v4.1.0 --to v3.9.7 --percent 5 --drain staged
routes pin --path /v1/chat --tag v3.9.7 --note "stabilize latency during change window"
```

sarah: executing now.

lin: tagging ops for customer comm draft. Small note only: "We applied a performance stabilization step during the change window to maintain consistent latency." No urgency.

ops_lead: I'll prepare the comm. Use "performance stabilization" language and include an opt-in escalation link. Also inform sales about scheduled demos in APAC.

deploy-bot: Rollout paused (r-98765). Withdraw started: 5 -> 0 (1 step). ETA ~30s. Action suppressed auto-rollback since operator is active.

sarah: Withdraw complete, pin applied. Route /v1/chat pinned to v3.9.7.

eng_runtime_oncall: Observing metrics — p95 trending down toward baseline, queue time improved. Good.

lin: Opening INC-7460, assigning to eng-runtime. Attach traces + canary payload. Also logging decision: soft withdraw to reduce customer churn and keep canary telemetry for forensics.

ops_lead: Sent customer note to #customer-comms. Copy: "During the scheduled change window we ran a stabilization step to ensure consistent latency. No action needed on your side. Reach out if you see regressions."

eng_runtime_oncall: For the postmortem add: root-cause hypothesis (scheduler contention), timeline (deploy -> alert -> pause -> withdraw -> pin), and the test matrix we'll add to CI to simulate short-request burst.

lin: Also note that automated rollback threshold remained enabled but was suppressed because a human operator intervened. That should be captured in audit and the release notes line.

ops_lead: I'll update release notes: "11:15 deploy to v4.1.0: temporary stabilization applied; canary withdrawn and route pinned to v3.9.7 pending investigation."

deploy-bot: Post-action summary: action=soft-withdraw, scope=canary, old=v3.9.7, attempted=v4.1.0, pinned=true, operator=sarah (1769999922).

lin: Thanks team. We'll reconvene at the 14:00 runtime triage if we don't have a quick root cause. Closing this thread — canary stable for now. :white_check_mark:
